content.text: {"title":"Attention Is All You Need: How the Transformer Works","steps":[{"title":"Why Drop Recurrence?","goal":"Show an RNN as a chain of hidden states h_t computed from h_{t-1} and the input at position t, so each step must wait for the previous one. Draw boxes in a row with arrows left to right on a short sentence and mark the sequential bottleneck, plus the long path between distant words."},{"title":"Encoder-Decoder Big Picture","goal":"Sketch the encoder mapping (x1..xn) to z=(z1..zn) and the decoder producing (y1..ym) one symbol at a time, auto-regressively, feeding earlier outputs back in. Draw two stacks of N=6 layers with an arrow from encoder to decoder, as in Figure 1."},{"title":"Queries, Keys, Values","goal":"Introduce attention as a query matched against keys to get weights over values, with the output a weighted sum. Use a tiny 3-word example with 2-d vectors and show the dot products of one query with each key, turning into weights."},{"title":"Scaled Dot-Product Attention","goal":"Write Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V and trace the matrix shapes on a small example. Explain why dividing by √d_k matters: dot products of d_k random components have variance d_k, which pushes softmax into flat-gradient regions."},{"title":"Multi-Head Attention","goal":"Show h=8 heads, each with learned projections W_i^Q, W_i^K, W_i^V down to d_k=d_v=64 from d_model=512, then concat and project with W^O. Draw parallel boxes merging into one, and explain that heads attend to different information, avoiding the averaging of a single head."},{"title":"Three Uses and Masking","goal":"Show the three attention types: encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention, and encoder-decoder attention, where queries come from the decoder and keys and values from the encoder. Draw a 4x4 grid with the upper triangle set to -∞ before softmax, so position i can't see later positions."},{"title":"Feed-Forward, Residuals, Norm","goal":"Write FFN(x)=max(0,xW1+b1)W2+b2 applied to each position separately, with 512→2048→512. Draw one layer as x flowing through a sub-layer with a skip connection into LayerNorm(x+Sublayer(x))."},{"title":"Embeddings and Positional Encoding","goal":"Explain that without recurrence the model has no sense of order, so sinusoidal vectors are added to the token embeddings: PE(pos,2i)=sin(pos/10000^{2i/d_model}), PE(pos,2i+1)=cos(...). Show a few dimensions of waves with different wavelengths for positions 0, 1, 2 and the sum with an embedding. Mention the final linear plus softmax producing next-token probabilities."},{"title":"Why Self-Attention Wins","goal":"Walk through Table 1 comparing self-attention, recurrent, and convolutional layers on complexity per layer, sequential operations, and maximum path length. Draw the path between the first and last word of a length-n sequence: O(1) for attention versus O(n) for an RNN."},{"title":"Training and Results","goal":"Briefly show the learning-rate schedule as a rise over 4000 warmup steps then inverse-sqrt decay, with dropout and label smoothing as regularizers. Then show the headline results: 28.4 BLEU on EN-DE and 41.8 on EN-FR at a fraction of the training cost."}],"coverPrompt":"A glowing web of luminous threads linking every bead on a long necklace to every other bead at once, with some threads brighter and thicker than others, set against a deep dark background in warm gold and blue."}
